data.body:
Root cause: the premise does not hold. Read-only evidence, 2026-11-18 PST, all times UTC on 2026-11-16:

- The polling agent's transcript (subagent a9b8657b2be12e91b) contains exactly 13 `gate_status` calls for job 1794856602730588534-4009502f…, from 19:18:10 to 19:22:04. That is a 4-minute window, not 60 minutes, and every call came BEFORE the run finished.
- The run ended at 19:24:31: GATE_PEAK_RSS elapsed_ms 449638; attestation signed_at 1794857058838360399 = 19:24:18. The production index file `/var/lib/docker/volumes/gerrit_mcp_code/_data/.rebar/gate_runs/<job>` was rewritten at 19:24:31 as `status: passed, verdict: PASS, sidecar_emitted: true`.
- No `gate_status` call was made after 19:24:31. The next call, at 19:25:50, was `plan_review_status`, which returned `certified`. So no poll made after the attestation existed ever returned `running`. Each `running` / `durable: unsigned` / `run-running` answer was correct when it was given.
- Re-test: my own 2 plan reviews today (jobs 1795027578…, 1795027647…). While running, `gate_status` matched the index file on the host; on the first poll after completion it returned `passed` with `durable` agreeing (`certified` for the PASS).

The same transcript did show a real, different `gate_status` defect: a false `failed / daemon-stopped` after an MCP blue-green cutover, twice on 2026-11-16. Filed as digestive-greasy-kingsnake.

Closing not_a_bug.
